honest_fail_comparison.readme_window_rule: last 20% of samples, window-mean Cd, gate |err| <= 3%
honest_fail_comparison.finding: All earlier rounds quote the same window-mean errors inside the README 3% gate ({"174": [2.7708], "202": [2.54, 2.77], "243": [2.54, 2.78]}), yet none of them emits an explicit 'VERDICT: PASS/FAIL' token and none carries a physical device line (/dev/tcaicardN, sdaa:N) for the judged run.  The recurring honest-FAIL is therefore a *process* failure (no machine-readable verdict + no device provenance), not a numerical gate failure; m202 additionally invented a stricter 'must hold over 3 rounds' criterion that the README does not contain (criterion drift, rejected here).
criterion_drift_rejected: m202: 'honest-FAIL because 3 rounds still not stably inside 3%' -- README gates on a single pre-registered reference and the two-tier monotone ladder, not on cross-round stability.
